output.normalized_title: order-service: Thread deadlock detected in OrderFulfillmentWorker (order-service)

output.classification_reasoning: The incident reports a thread deadlock within the OrderFulfillmentWorker of the order-service. A deadlock is an internal application logic/concurrency issue rather than a network, authentication, database, or storage problem, aligning with the 'application_error' category. Resolving deadlocks typically requires code analysis, lock ordering review, and possibly redesign of concurrency primitives, which involves moderate engineering effort and cross‑team coordination, but does not usually demand extensive infrastructure changes. Hence the apparent operational complexity is assessed as Moderate.

prerequisites: Root access or AWS SSO role ProdOperations
output.security_notes: Do not terminate primary node without promoting read-replica first. Verify write freeze before reboot.

diagnostic_stage_assessment.notes: Current incident matches historical thread deadlock pattern across multiple services, indicating a systemic issue.

output.governing_sla_rule: Tier-1 service impacting >= 500 users, or cross-tier impact >= 2,000 users.
output.justification: The incident affects 3,500 users on a Tier-1 service, far exceeding the 500‑user threshold defined for SEV-2. The outage duration of 43 minutes is within the typical response window for SEV-2 (under 1 hour) and does not meet the higher urgency criteria of SEV-1 (which requires immediate, high‑impact service loss or regulatory breach). The diagnostic stage is at Root Cause Confirmed with high confidence (0.94), confirming the impact scope. Therefore, according to the deterministic rule, the appropriate severity is SEV-2.

remediation_steps.title: Validate Access and Kubernetes Context
remediation_steps.description: Confirm that the operator has the required ProdOperations SSO role and that kubectl is pointed at the production cluster in us-east-1.
verification: AWS identity ARN includes ProdOperations role
kubectl context equals prod-us-east-1
Node list shows expected production node names

remediation_steps.title: Enforce Write Freeze and Promote Read‑Replica
remediation_steps.description: Prevent new writes to the primary database, promote the healthy read‑replica to primary, and verify replication status before any node restarts.
commands: kubectl exec -n database primary-db-pod -- /bin/sh -c "psql -c \"ALTER SYSTEM SET default_transaction_read_only = on;\""
verification: Primary DB reports read‑only mode
Replica reports NOT in recovery (i.e., promoted)
Replication lag metrics drop to < 1 second

remediation_steps.title: Graceful Rolling Restart of Affected Services
remediation_steps.description: Trigger a rolling restart of the deployments that experienced the thread deadlock to clear stale worker state.
verification: All pods in both deployments reach READY=1/1
No CrashLoopBackOff events in recent logs
Thread pool metrics return to normal levels

remediation_steps.title: Reboot Primary Database Node (if required)
remediation_steps.description: After confirming the replica is now primary, safely reboot the former primary node to clear any kernel‑level deadlock state.
commands: aws ssm send-command --instance-ids i-xxxxxxxxxxxx --document-name AWS-RunShellScript --parameters commands=['sudo reboot'] --region us-east-1
verification: Node reports status 'running' after reboot
Database service health endpoint returns 200 OK
Replication topology shows single primary with healthy replica

remediation_steps.title: Post‑Remediation Health Audit
remediation_steps.description: Run synthetic health checks and verify that error rates have returned to baseline across all impacted services.
commands: kubectl logs -l app=order-service --since=5m | grep ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_925 || true
kubectl logs -l app=inventory-api --since=5m | grep ERR_APPLICATION_ERROR_444 || true
verification: Both health endpoints return status OK
No occurrences of the listed error signatures in recent logs
Monitoring dashboards show error rate < 1% of baseline

rollback_plan.overall_strategy: Revert all service deployments to the previous stable image tag, demote the promoted replica back to read‑only, and re‑enable writes on the original primary node if it remains healthy.

steps.description: Undo rolling restarts by rolling back to the prior container image tag.
verification: Pods return to previous image version
READY=1/1 for all rolled‑back pods

steps.description: Demote the promoted replica and re‑promote the original primary (if still reachable).
commands: kubectl exec -n database primary-db-pod -- /bin/sh -c "psql -c \"ALTER SYSTEM SET default_transaction_read_only = off;\""
verification: Original primary reports NOT in recovery
Replica reports IN recovery (read‑only)
Writes are accepted on the original primary

steps.description: Remove write freeze from the primary database and confirm normal write traffic.
commands: kubectl exec -n database primary-db-pod -- /bin/sh -c "psql -c \"ALTER SYSTEM SET default_transaction_read_only = off;\""
verification: Primary DB reports read_only = off
Write‑test endpoint returns success

verification_checkpoints: All services report health OK after rollback
Error signature counts remain at pre‑incident baseline
Database replication topology restored to original state

prerequisite_checks: Operator credentials verified for ProdOperations SSO role
Rollback procedure documented in runbook RB-106
Write freeze confirmed before any primary node reboot
